title: Stably free invertible modules are free
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module. Suppose $M$ is invertible, meaning that the canonical evaluation $M^\vee\otimes_R M\to R$ is bijective, and stably free, meaning that some finite free $R$-module $Q$ has $M\oplus Q$ free [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Then $M$ is free.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Module.free_of_isStablyFree_of_invertible. For the zero ring all modules are free. Otherwise write M direct sum Q free, put n=rank Q and use rank one at a prime to identify rank(M direct sum Q)=n+1. The top exterior power is free of rank one. Cofactor expansion along M defines a surjection from this rank-one free module onto M; invertibility makes this surjection bijective. This produces the desired basis. The installed Mathlib file proves this directly.
